answer: Florida Medicaid covers up to a 34-day supply of drugs, per prescription, when prescribed by a licensed practitioner. You can get up to a 100-day supply of prescribed drugs, per prescription, when a drug has been designated by AHCA as a maintenance drug and published on the AHCA Web site. The passages do not state whether your specific blood pressure medicine is designated as a maintenance drug.

citations.quote: Florida Medicaid covers up to a 34-day supply of drugs, per prescription, in accordance with section 409.912, F.S., or as specified in this policy when prescribed by a licensed practitioner

Up to a 100-day supply of prescribed drugs, per prescription, when a drug has been designated by AHCA as a maintenance drug and published on the AHCA Web site at http://www.ahca.myflorida.com/medicaid/Policy_and_Quality/Policy/pharmacy_p olicy/index.shtml.

gold_answer: Yes, in some cases. The standard limit is a 34-day supply, but Florida Medicaid covers up to a 100-day supply per prescription when AHCA has designated the drug as a maintenance drug and published it on its website.
gold_quote: Florida Medicaid covers more than a 34-day supply of prescribed drugs as follows: − Up to a 100-day supply of prescribed drugs, per prescription, when a drug has been designated by AHCA as a maintenance drug

judge.rationale: The answer gives the 34-day standard limit and the 100-day supply for drugs AHCA designates as maintenance drugs and publishes on its website, matching the gold answer, and every claim appears in passages P1 and P3.

question: My pharmacy says Florida Medicaid only ever gives a month of pills at a time. Is there any way to get my blood pressure medicine for three months?
